questions.passage: In aquarium trials, a species of sea anemone tolerated water temperatures between 18°C and 25°C without measurable loss of the algae living in its tissues. At 27°C and 28°C, however, the anemones lost much of that algae within two days. The researchers did not test intermediate temperatures and do not know whether the response begins gradually or abruptly. Thus, ______
questions.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: the anemones lose algae only when water reaches exactly 28°C.
choices.B: the anemones will never lose algae at any temperature below 27°C.
choices.C: algal loss must increase by the same amount for every one-degree rise in temperature.
choices.D: a substantial change occurs somewhere between the tested temperature ranges, but its precise onset cannot be determined from these trials.

questions.explanation: Loss is absent at up to 25°C and substantial at 27°C and above, leaving the transition location and shape unresolved.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: Algal loss was also observed at 27°C.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: Untested temperatures between 25°C and 27°C might already produce loss.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: The evidence does not establish a linear response or sample intermediate values.
choice_explanations.D: Correct: Loss is absent at up to 25°C and substantial at 27°C and above, leaving the transition location and shape unresolved.

evidence_quotes: between 18°C and 25°C without measurable loss
At 27°C and 28°C, however
did not test intermediate temperatures
questions.strategy: Do not infer continuity, slope, or exact threshold when only a few points are measured.

questions.passage: A series of parallel grooves in an ancient riverbed could have been made by animals dragging their tails while walking, or by floating branches scraping the bottom during a flood. The grooves are similar in width and spacing, and neither clear footprints nor associated wood fragments have been preserved. Both mechanisms have produced comparable marks in modern sediment experiments.
questions.question: Which choice is best supported by the text?

choices.A: The experiments demonstrate that grooves with the observed pattern could not have formed naturally.
choices.B: The grooves definitely record the movements of tail-dragging animals because they appear in parallel lines.
choices.C: The grooves definitely resulted from a flood because no footprints were preserved.
choices.D: Without additional diagnostic evidence, the grooves alone cannot establish whether animals or branches produced them.

questions.explanation: Two mechanisms independently reproduce the same traces, and distinguishing remains are absent.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: Both suggested mechanisms are natural and reproduced similar marks.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: Parallel grooves are also compatible with dragged branches.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: Footprints could have failed to preserve even if animals made the grooves.
choice_explanations.D: Correct: Two mechanisms independently reproduce the same traces, and distinguishing remains are absent.

evidence_quotes: Both mechanisms have produced comparable marks in modern sediment experiments
neither clear footprints nor associated wood fragments have been preserved
questions.strategy: When two competing explanations predict the observed outcome, withhold a unique identification.

questions.passage: After a city installed new signs advertising its free adult-literacy classes, visits to the enrollment website doubled. The number of new students attending at least four sessions, however, stayed nearly unchanged. A program administrator argues that the advertising was ineffective, while a colleague notes that website visits reflect initial interest rather than sustained participation. Based on the text, the colleague would most likely agree that ______
questions.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: the website-visit data conclusively show that the literacy classes became less effective at teaching students.
choices.B: all visitors to the enrollment website had already completed the literacy course.
choices.C: greater visibility of the classes need not translate into a corresponding increase in sustained attendance.
choices.D: a doubling of website visits guarantees twice as many students will finish the course.

questions.explanation: Website interest increased without a matching rise in sustained student participation.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: Visits do not measure instructional effectiveness.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: The passage gives no visitor-level history.
choice_explanations.C: Correct: Website interest increased without a matching rise in sustained student participation.
choice_explanations.D: Incorrect: Sustained attendance remained nearly unchanged.

evidence_quotes: visits to the enrollment website doubled
number of new students attending at least four sessions, however, stayed nearly unchanged
questions.strategy: Differentiate leading indicators or attention metrics from the outcome of interest.

questions.passage: A restoration project reintroduced reeds to a damaged marsh and also reopened a channel that allowed periodic tidal flooding. Fish populations increased in the restored area. In a later test, workers temporarily blocked the channel while leaving the reeds intact; the fish increase stopped. Some observers concluded that reeds had played no role in the initial recovery. A project biologist, however, noted that reeds provide shelter only when enough water reaches them.
questions.question: Based on the text, which statement would the biologist most likely agree with?

choices.A: The fish increase proves that reeds alone can restore the marsh even without tidal water.
choices.B: Neither reeds nor tidal flooding can affect fish populations because the restoration used both at once.
choices.C: The blocked channel shows that water access matters, but it does not establish that the reeds were irrelevant when both measures operated together.
choices.D: The channel experiment demonstrates that removing reeds would have no effect while tides are restored.

questions.explanation: The intervention tests one needed condition but cannot eliminate a possible interaction with sheltering reeds.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: The fish increase stopped when the channel was blocked.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: The experiment supplies evidence that water access matters, though the reeds’ separate contribution remains unmeasured.
choice_explanations.C: Correct: The intervention tests one needed condition but cannot eliminate a possible interaction with sheltering reeds.
choice_explanations.D: Incorrect: The experiment altered water access, not the presence of reeds.

evidence_quotes: the fish increase stopped
reeds provide shelter only when enough water reaches them
questions.strategy: A failed outcome after removing one factor shows that factor may be required, not that every remaining factor is useless.

questions.passage: When a small dam was removed from a mountain river, gravel began accumulating in the former reservoir within months. Spawning fish remained scarce during the first two seasons but became noticeably more abundant in the third and fourth seasons, after gravel beds had stabilized. Scientists note that these fish typically need stable gravel to reproduce successfully. The observations suggest that ______
questions.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: removing any dam will guarantee increased fish populations after exactly three seasons.
choices.B: benefits for the spawning fish may appear only after the habitat changes initiated by dam removal have had time to develop.
choices.C: dam removal reduced spawning opportunities in the long term because fish were initially scarce.
choices.D: the fish increase must have occurred before gravel began accumulating.

questions.explanation: Habitat changes preceded the delayed population response, consistent with reproduction depending on stable gravel.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: The record concerns one river and does not establish a universal timeline.
choice_explanations.B: Correct: Habitat changes preceded the delayed population response, consistent with reproduction depending on stable gravel.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: Fish later increased as the gravel beds stabilized.
choice_explanations.D: Incorrect: The passage gives the opposite sequence.

evidence_quotes: gravel began accumulating
became noticeably more abundant in the third and fourth seasons
need stable gravel
questions.strategy: Check whether an intervention’s expected outcome requires an intermediate process that takes time.

questions.passage: A biologist suspects that birds near highways sing at higher pitches because traffic noise masks lower notes. Another researcher proposes that artificial streetlights, not traffic, cause the change. Along several roads where lighting levels remain nearly constant throughout the week, average song pitch falls on quiet Sundays and rises again during busy weekday mornings.
questions.question: Based on the text, which statement would the biologist most likely agree with?

choices.A: Higher traffic levels always cause every individual bird to sing at precisely the same pitch.
choices.B: The birds change pitch only because their species composition changes between Sunday and Monday.
choices.C: Streetlights are definitely the sole cause of the pitch change because they remain in place all week.
choices.D: Variation in traffic noise contributes to song pitch, although the observations do not exclude every other influence.

questions.explanation: Pitch covaries with traffic while lighting is relatively stable, which favors the noise hypothesis without proving it exclusive.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: Average changes do not establish identical individual behavior.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: No change in species composition is documented.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: A factor that remains nearly constant does not readily explain a recurring day-specific change.
choice_explanations.D: Correct: Pitch covaries with traffic while lighting is relatively stable, which favors the noise hypothesis without proving it exclusive.

evidence_quotes: lighting levels remain nearly constant throughout the week
song pitch falls on quiet Sundays and rises again during busy weekday mornings
questions.strategy: Use variation in one factor against stability in a rival to weigh explanations without overstating causality.

questions.passage: Four medieval chronicles describe an eclipse on the same date, apparently supporting the reliability of the event's dating. A historian notices, however, that all four manuscripts reproduce an unusual spelling mistake in the name of the observing town. Archival analysis reveals that three of the manuscripts were copied from a version of the fourth. The evidence implies that ______
questions.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: the manuscripts must have been written by four people who independently observed the eclipse.
choices.B: the shared mistake proves that the eclipse itself was invented.
choices.C: the earliest version can be dated precisely from the error in the town’s name alone.
choices.D: four surviving accounts need not constitute four independent confirmations of the eclipse date.

questions.explanation: Three copies inherit information from a common source, reducing the effective number of independent testimonies.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: Three texts were copied from a common source.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: Copying can produce dependent accounts of a real event; no falsification is established.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: A shared spelling mistake does not supply a calendar date.
choice_explanations.D: Correct: Three copies inherit information from a common source, reducing the effective number of independent testimonies.

evidence_quotes: three of the manuscripts were copied from a version of the fourth
questions.strategy: Track whether apparently separate pieces of evidence share an origin before treating them as independent.

questions.passage: A museum emailed visitors an optional survey about a recent exhibition, and 84 percent of respondents rated it excellent. Visitors were most likely to open the survey after receiving a follow-up message from the exhibition's membership club, whose subscribers frequently attend museum events. The museum did not record ratings from people who ignored the invitation. A statistician warns that ______
questions.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: membership club subscribers must have visited the exhibition fewer times than other visitors.
choices.B: the excellent ratings must be higher than those of nonrespondents because the survey reached frequent museum attendees.
choices.C: exactly 84 percent of all people who attended the exhibition must have found it excellent.
choices.D: it is uncertain whether the high rating among respondents reflects the views of all exhibition visitors.

questions.explanation: The responding group may overrepresent highly engaged visitors, while nonrespondents remain unknown.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: Subscribers are described as frequent museum attendees, and no specific visit counts are given.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: Engaged attendees may be overrepresented, but nonrespondents’ ratings are unknown, so a definite comparison is unsupported.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: The percentage applies only to respondents, whose participation was selective.
choice_explanations.D: Correct: The responding group may overrepresent highly engaged visitors, while nonrespondents remain unknown.

evidence_quotes: optional survey
membership club, whose subscribers frequently attend museum events
did not record ratings from people who ignored the invitation
questions.strategy: Ask who had a higher probability of responding before generalizing a sample percentage.

questions.passage: Engineers coated a moving metal component with a thin film containing microscopic water-attracting particles. Under humid laboratory conditions, coated components experienced substantially less friction than uncoated ones. Under dry conditions, the coated and uncoated components performed similarly. The engineers hypothesize that moisture enables the particles to form a lubricating layer.
questions.question: Which choice is best supported by the text?

choices.A: The particles’ exact molecular mechanism has been proven by the friction measurements alone.
choices.B: The coating’s friction-reducing benefit is associated with humid conditions rather than appearing uniformly in all tested environments.
choices.C: The coating substantially reduces friction even when no moisture is available.
choices.D: The coating permanently changes the metal so that friction can never increase again.

questions.explanation: A benefit appears in the humid treatment but not the dry treatment; the proposed microphysical explanation remains a hypothesis.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: The moisture-driven lubrication mechanism is a hypothesis; friction measurements do not directly establish molecular details.
choice_explanations.B: Correct: A benefit appears in the humid treatment but not the dry treatment; the proposed microphysical explanation remains a hypothesis.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: Dry-condition tests showed similar friction with and without coating.
choice_explanations.D: Incorrect: Neither a permanent material change nor future performance was measured.

evidence_quotes: Under humid laboratory conditions, coated components experienced substantially less friction
Under dry conditions, the coated and uncoated components performed similarly
questions.strategy: Identify the observed treatment-by-condition interaction while keeping the proposed mechanism provisional.

validation.editorial_note: Mechanical checks cannot formally prove that all distractors are logically impossible; content has been written and manually reviewed for uniqueness of the best-supported answer.

metadata.affiliation: Independent study resource. Not affiliated with College Board.

This is a non-exhaustive qualitative survey; no official question or explanation is copied.
source_scan.source_count_caveat: Keyword-based count from answer explanations is an indicative sample and not a full official skill-category classification.

reviewed_anchor_examples.rule: No punctuation between a preposition and its complement
Paired punctuation around supplementary appositive material
Colon introducing an explanatory phrase after an independent clause
Do not separate noun title and identifying proper noun
Direct versus indirect questions and appropriate end punctuation
Punctuation of a supplemental phrase after a clause
No punctuation between a subject and its main verb
Semicolon between independent clauses, then introductory comma

Matched em dashes around supplementary material

source_scan.question_bank_relationship: Skill-pattern resemblance only. All names, scenarios, passages, options, and solutions are newly written.

patterns.description: Separate two independent clauses with a semicolon; reject comma splices and fragments after a semicolon.
patterns.strategy: Identify the subject and finite verb on both sides; a semicolon can separate independent clauses without a coordinating conjunction.

patterns.description: End a complete thought and begin an independent sentence without creating a splice or misusing a colon.
patterns.strategy: Check whether each side can stand alone; use a period when the second sentence is a new topic rather than an explanation of the first.

patterns.description: Join two independent clauses with a comma before a coordinating conjunction.
patterns.strategy: Locate the subjects and verbs on both sides; if but/and/yet/or links two independent clauses, the comma normally precedes the conjunction.

patterns.description: Use a comma after a subordinate clause that precedes an independent clause.
patterns.strategy: A clause introduced by although, if, because, or when cannot stand alone; place a comma at its boundary with the following main clause.

patterns.description: Use a colon after an independent clause to introduce a list, renaming phrase, or explanation.
patterns.strategy: Verify that the material before the colon is a complete clause; check that the material after it supplies the promised list or explanation.

patterns.description: Do not separate a verb from its complement, a preposition from its object, or a subject from its predicate.
patterns.strategy: Find the grammatical core: punctuation cannot split a verb from what completes it, a preposition from its object, or a subject from its verb.

patterns.description: Close a nonessential appositive or relative clause with a matching comma.
patterns.strategy: Remove the parenthetical phrase; if the remaining sentence is complete, use a matching comma to close the interruption.

patterns.description: Keep an essential that/whose modifier attached to the noun it identifies.
patterns.strategy: A clause specifying which one is meant is essential; do not insert a comma before restrictive that or leave an unmatched comma before the main verb.

patterns.description: Use matching em dashes around a mid-sentence nonessential interruption.
patterns.strategy: Find the opening em dash, then close the supplementary phrase with a second em dash before the main sentence resumes.

patterns.description: Punctuate two independent clauses joined by however, therefore, instead, or nevertheless.
patterns.strategy: A conjunctive adverb is not a coordinating conjunction: separate independent clauses with a semicolon and follow the adverb with a comma.

patterns.description: Use semicolons between list items that already contain internal commas.
patterns.strategy: Mentally bracket each full list item, including its description; use semicolons consistently to prevent item boundaries from blending with internal commas.

patterns.description: Close a directly asked question with a question mark before the next sentence.
patterns.strategy: Ask whether the first clause directly asks a question, as opposed to reporting a question; use a question mark for a direct question.

questions.passage: The oldest wax seals in the collection bear an image of a crescent_______ seals from the same workshop made a century later depict a six-pointed star.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.B: ; although
choices.D: , however,

questions.explanation: Both sides are independent clauses, and the semicolon cleanly separates two contrasting observations about seals from different periods.

choice_explanations.A: Correct: Both sides are independent clauses, and the semicolon cleanly separates two contrasting observations about seals from different periods.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: Although makes the material after the semicolon dependent, leaving a fragment instead of an independent clause.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: A comma alone cannot join the complete clauses beginning “The oldest wax seals” and “seals from the same workshop.”
choice_explanations.D: Incorrect: However is a conjunctive adverb, not a conjunction; the comma before it produces a comma splice.

evidence_quotes: The oldest wax seals in the collection bear an image of a crescent
seals from the same workshop made a century later depict a six-pointed star.
questions.strategy: Identify the subject and finite verb on both sides; a semicolon can separate independent clauses without a coordinating conjunction.
questions.corrected_text: The oldest wax seals in the collection bear an image of a crescent; seals from the same workshop made a century later depict a six-pointed star.
questions.rule: Separate two independent clauses with a semicolon; reject comma splices and fragments after a semicolon.

questions.passage: Despite months of adjustments to its cooling system, the prototype remained stable during repeated laboratory trials_______ its performance varied sharply once it was exposed to saltwater.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: ; because
choices.B: , however,

questions.explanation: The first clause reports laboratory stability, whereas the second reports an independent, contrasting field observation; a semicolon properly joins them.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: The because-clause after the semicolon cannot stand alone; a semicolon requires another independent clause.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: The inserted conjunctive adverb does not repair the comma splice between the two main clauses.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: The two complete clauses cannot be joined by a comma alone.
choice_explanations.D: Correct: The first clause reports laboratory stability, whereas the second reports an independent, contrasting field observation; a semicolon properly joins them.

evidence_quotes: nts to its cooling system, the prototype remained stable during repeated laboratory trials
its performance varied sharply once it was exposed to saltwater.
questions.strategy: Identify the subject and finite verb on both sides; a semicolon can separate independent clauses without a coordinating conjunction.
questions.corrected_text: Despite months of adjustments to its cooling system, the prototype remained stable during repeated laboratory trials; its performance varied sharply once it was exposed to saltwater.
questions.rule: Separate two independent clauses with a semicolon; reject comma splices and fragments after a semicolon.

questions.passage: After conservators had cleaned and photographed the recovered fragments, every tile in the first mosaic was carefully numbered_______ the pieces from the second mosaic were cataloged only by color.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: ; whereas
choices.D: , moreover,

questions.explanation: The sentence contains two complete statements describing different cataloging practices, making a semicolon appropriate.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: Whereas introduces a subordinate clause, which cannot appear on its own after this semicolon.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: A comma by itself joins two independent clauses incorrectly.
choice_explanations.C: Correct: The sentence contains two complete statements describing different cataloging practices, making a semicolon appropriate.
choice_explanations.D: Incorrect: Adding moreover between commas does not supply the independent-clause boundary required here.

evidence_quotes: hotographed the recovered fragments, every tile in the first mosaic was carefully numbered
the pieces from the second mosaic were cataloged only by color.
questions.strategy: Identify the subject and finite verb on both sides; a semicolon can separate independent clauses without a coordinating conjunction.
questions.corrected_text: After conservators had cleaned and photographed the recovered fragments, every tile in the first mosaic was carefully numbered; the pieces from the second mosaic were cataloged only by color.
questions.rule: Separate two independent clauses with a semicolon; reject comma splices and fragments after a semicolon.

questions.passage: Despite the stations being only twenty kilometers apart, the station recorded heavy rainfall throughout March_______ the neighboring station reported unusually dry conditions for the same period.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.C: , instead,
choices.D: ; while

questions.explanation: Each station is the subject of a complete clause, and the semicolon separates the contrasting reports without changing their relationship.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: A lone comma results in a comma splice between the two reports.
choice_explanations.B: Correct: Each station is the subject of a complete clause, and the semicolon separates the contrasting reports without changing their relationship.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: The phrase instead, offset only by commas, still leaves two independent clauses improperly joined.
choice_explanations.D: Incorrect: While would subordinate the second report, leaving a fragment after a semicolon.

evidence_quotes: s being only twenty kilometers apart, the station recorded heavy rainfall throughout March
the neighboring station reported unusually dry conditions for the same period.
questions.strategy: Identify the subject and finite verb on both sides; a semicolon can separate independent clauses without a coordinating conjunction.
questions.corrected_text: Despite the stations being only twenty kilometers apart, the station recorded heavy rainfall throughout March; the neighboring station reported unusually dry conditions for the same period.
questions.rule: Separate two independent clauses with a semicolon; reject comma splices and fragments after a semicolon.

questions.passage: The pond's salinity remained constant across the observation _______ A separate team later documented the nesting habits of birds on the surrounding cliffs.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: period:
choices.B: period.
choices.C: period,
choices.D: period

questions.explanation: A period ends the complete salinity statement and allows the unrelated account of the bird study to begin as a new sentence.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: The bird-nesting report does not define, explain, or enumerate the unchanged salinity, so a colon would misrepresent the relationship.
choice_explanations.B: Correct: A period ends the complete salinity statement and allows the unrelated account of the bird study to begin as a new sentence.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: A comma alone splices two independent sentences.
choice_explanations.D: Incorrect: Without terminal punctuation, the sentences run together.

evidence_quotes: The pond's salinity remained constant across the observation
A separate team later documented the nesting habits of birds on the surrounding cliffs.
questions.strategy: Check whether each side can stand alone; use a period when the second sentence is a new topic rather than an explanation of the first.
questions.corrected_text: The pond's salinity remained constant across the observation period. A separate team later documented the nesting habits of birds on the surrounding cliffs.
questions.rule: End a complete thought and begin an independent sentence without creating a splice or misusing a colon.

questions.passage: The manuscript's final page was missing from the _______ A separate investigation examined pigments used in its cover illustration.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: archive.
choices.B: archive,
choices.C: archive
choices.D: archive:

questions.explanation: The missing-page statement is complete; the next independent sentence introduces a different inquiry, so a period marks the boundary.

choice_explanations.A: Correct: The missing-page statement is complete; the next independent sentence introduces a different inquiry, so a period marks the boundary.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: A comma alone cannot join these two complete statements.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: The second independent clause begins without any sentence-boundary punctuation.
choice_explanations.D: Incorrect: The examination of cover pigments does not explain or list the circumstances of the missing last page.

evidence_quotes: The manuscript's final page was missing from the
A separate investigation examined pigments used in its cover illustration.
questions.strategy: Check whether each side can stand alone; use a period when the second sentence is a new topic rather than an explanation of the first.
questions.corrected_text: The manuscript's final page was missing from the archive. A separate investigation examined pigments used in its cover illustration.
questions.rule: End a complete thought and begin an independent sentence without creating a splice or misusing a colon.

questions.passage: A survey of the island's eastern slope identified three abandoned _______ Another expedition later mapped ocean currents beyond the island's reefs.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: quarries,
choices.B: quarries:
choices.C: quarries
choices.D: quarries.

questions.explanation: The quarry survey is a complete statement, and the later study of ocean currents is a separate topic that needs a new sentence.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: The comma alone creates a comma splice between complete sentences.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: The ocean-current study is not a list or explanation of the three quarries, so the colon signals the wrong relationship.
choice_explanations.C: Incorrect: Two independent clauses have been fused without punctuation.
choice_explanations.D: Correct: The quarry survey is a complete statement, and the later study of ocean currents is a separate topic that needs a new sentence.

evidence_quotes: A survey of the island's eastern slope identified three abandoned
Another expedition later mapped ocean currents beyond the island's reefs.
questions.strategy: Check whether each side can stand alone; use a period when the second sentence is a new topic rather than an explanation of the first.
questions.corrected_text: A survey of the island's eastern slope identified three abandoned quarries. Another expedition later mapped ocean currents beyond the island's reefs.
questions.rule: End a complete thought and begin an independent sentence without creating a splice or misusing a colon.

questions.passage: The observatory replaced its original tracking mechanism in _______ A later report examined how the site's radio antennas had been maintained in the 1980s.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The replacement date completes the first sentence; the report on antenna maintenance begins a distinct independent sentence.

choice_explanations.A: Incorrect: The report on antennas is not an explanation or specification of the earlier tracking-mechanism replacement.
choice_explanations.B: Incorrect: Without a period or other appropriate separator, the sentences form a run-on.
choice_explanations.C: Correct: The replacement date completes the first sentence; the report on antenna maintenance begins a distinct independent sentence.
choice_explanations.D: Incorrect: The comma would improperly combine two independent clauses.

evidence_quotes: The observatory replaced its original tracking mechanism in
A later report examined how the site's radio antennas had been maintained in the 1980s.
questions.strategy: Check whether each side can stand alone; use a period when the second sentence is a new topic rather than an explanation of the first.
questions.corrected_text: The observatory replaced its original tracking mechanism in 1974. A later report examined how the site's radio antennas had been maintained in the 1980s.
questions.rule: End a complete thought and begin an independent sentence without creating a splice or misusing a colon.

questions.passage: In a study designed to minimize differences among samples, the trial used identical glass containers_______ the vessels at the edge of the shelf heated more quickly.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: but
choices.B: ; but,
choices.C: , but
choices.D: , but,

questions.explanation: But joins the independent clause about identical containers with the contrasting independent clause about unequal heating; a comma precedes it.

patterns.description: Choose plural and possessive forms that reflect exactly how many people or groups own something.
patterns.strategy: Count the possessors first, then decide where the apostrophe belongs.

patterns.description: Choose the determiner (its/their, this/these) matching the noun or antecedent in number.
patterns.strategy: Identify the specific noun being modified and trace the determiner to its owner or referent.

patterns.description: Match independent or reflexive pronouns to the number and role of their referents.
patterns.strategy: Underline the exact noun that the pronoun replaces; check singular/plural and reflexive meaning.

patterns.description: Match a finite verb to its real subject despite intervening prepositional or relative phrases.
patterns.strategy: Strip out phrases between the subject and verb and test subject-verb agreement.

patterns.description: Match a verb to a subject placed after the verb in inverted or locative constructions.
patterns.strategy: Find the subject after the blank; do not let a fronted location phrase dictate verb number.

patterns.description: Maintain a tense that agrees with an explicit time frame and neighboring verbs.
patterns.strategy: Use dates and words such as now, every year, and in 19XX to pick the appropriate finite tense.

patterns.description: Use a past-perfect verb for a completed event that precedes another past event.
patterns.strategy: Put the events on a timeline; the event completed before a past reference point takes had + past participle.

patterns.description: Supply a finite main verb when another phrase is introductory or modifying.
patterns.strategy: Locate the main-clause subject; participles and infinitives alone cannot serve as its finite predicate.

patterns.description: Use participles or infinitives in supplementary, relative, or purpose phrases without adding an independent verb.
patterns.strategy: Ask whether the blank is a modifier or purpose phrase, not an extra finite verb.

patterns.description: Place the noun actually described immediately after an introductory modifier or comparison.
patterns.strategy: Name who or what the introductory phrase describes; that noun must be the grammatical subject after it.

patterns.description: Choose a relative form and a finite verb that completes a relative clause and agrees with its antecedent.
patterns.strategy: After who, which, or that, check whether the clause has a finite verb and whether it agrees with the preceding noun.

patterns.description: Maintain the same required verb form in coordinated verbs, especially after a modal or infinitival marker.
patterns.strategy: Read the shared helper (can, would, should, to) across every coordinated action.
